significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that, for content-matched problems, increasing framed questioner status monotonically increases thinking-token allocation independently of difficulty, together with the form-(ii) mechanism that a "status-sensitive effort-budget representation read at the prompt boundary" causally mediates that effect. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, and it would constrain explanations of test-time compute allocation used in work such as s1's budget forcing (Muennighoff et al., 2025), although the causal representation-plus-steering component remains bounded mainly to one behavior: reasoning length and its associated accuracy disparity. The negative branch would meaningfully rule out status as an effort-allocation signal in the asserted model class, but would not rule out other socially induced biases or other internal budget mechanisms, so this is a sharp but non-load-bearing facet of efficient reasoning. In the topic-substitution check, efficient-reasoning interpretability alone would not earn this score; the specific status-conditioned ordering and its dissociation from true difficulty supply the above-median increment.

reach.justification: The claim hands over two named handles: "effort parity" as an audit metric and a "training-free debiasing steer" that can equalize status-conditioned compute allocation. The audit can be applied ex ante to screen a reasoning model before deployment, while the steer acts before generation, giving auditors or education, healthcare, and enterprise deployers an action window rather than merely explaining completed failures. After model-specific re-extraction, the substantive prediction—"different status cue, different think-token distribution" with an ordered status effect—remains a relation to check across tasks and status ladders, although the claim's acknowledgment that effects may be model-family-specific limits stronger universal transfer. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic efficient-reasoning research would not itself provide a status-parity audit or deployment-time equity control.
